finding: The selected two-code point endpoint is byte-identical, including relative branches. Both read-consumer loops still make four two-argument indirect calls and assemble the results in registers; stack offsets, register allocation and instruction placement differ. This rules out added inner-kernel instructions, but does not identify the cause of the cross-binary timing difference.
decision: Retain the observed AVX2 tail as an unresolved cross-binary control difference; use one ordinary four-row packet for this consumer, which is roughly twice as fast as current repeated points. Do not duplicate the identical point kernel.
